description: The Weaver live-check findings of level 'violation' that are known and are not about what Grot's Pizzeria does itself: what the runtimes and the frameworks emit about themselves, which does not match the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions registry (yet). Every other violation fails the check (see tests/GrotsPizzeria.EndToEndTests/WeaverReportTests.cs), so what the sample emits itself (the HTTP server and client telemetry, the database spans, the grot.* signals and the application logs) has to be clean. An allowance is for one thing only, and says why: add to it with care.

allowances.name: aspnetcore.identity.*
allowances.reason: ASP.NET Core Identity's own metrics have an attribute (aspnetcore.authentication.is_persistent) that the registry does not have yet.

allowances.name: aspnetcore.components.*
allowances.reason: Blazor's own metrics (what it renders, handles and navigates to), which the UI gets from the framework, are not in the registry yet.

allowances.name: Event *
allowances.reason: Blazor's own spans for the events of a component have attributes (aspnetcore.components.*) that are not in the registry yet.

allowances.name: Route *
allowances.reason: Blazor's own spans for navigating to a component have attributes (aspnetcore.components.*) that are not in the registry yet.

allowances.name: dotnet.gc.*
allowances.reason: The .NET garbage collector's metrics name the generation gc.heap.generation, where the registry says dotnet.gc.heap.generation.

allowances.name: http.client.request.time_in_queue
allowances.reason: HttpClient's own metric of how long a request waited for a connection is not in the registry.

allowances.name: otlp.exporter.*
allowances.reason: The OpenTelemetry .NET SDK's metrics about its own OTLP exporter are not in the registry.

allowances.name: processedLogs
allowances.reason: The OpenTelemetry Java SDK's metrics about its own log processors are named in a way that the conventions do not allow.

allowances.name: processedSpans
allowances.reason: The OpenTelemetry Java SDK's metrics about its own span processors are named in a way that the conventions do not allow.

allowances.name: queueSize
allowances.reason: The OpenTelemetry Java SDK's metric of the size of its own processors' queues is named in a way that the conventions do not allow.

allowances.name: v8js.memory.heap.*
allowances.reason: Node.js's V8 heap metrics are gauges, where the registry says that they are up-down counters.

allowances.name: * http receive
allowances.reason: FastAPI's ASGI instrumentation makes internal spans for the events of a request, with an attribute (asgi.event.type) that is not in the registry.

allowances.name: * http send
allowances.reason: FastAPI's ASGI instrumentation makes internal spans for the events of a request, with an attribute (asgi.event.type) that is not in the registry.

allowances.name: request handler - *
allowances.reason: Express's instrumentation makes internal spans for its handlers, with attributes (express.name and express.type) that are not in the registry.
The Python and Java auto-instrumentation say which version of it made the telemetry, which is not in the registry.

ASP.NET Core Data Protection logs a warning, with the id of the key (KeyId) that it created, the first time that it runs with no keys (such as a new volume, or CI). The attribute is not in the registry.
ASP.NET Core Data Protection warns that its keys are stored without encryption, which is the case for the sample's volume, and its named events are not in the registry.
ASP.NET Core's hosting logs have attributes named for the URLs that the application listens on, which are not in the registry.
